transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because after my late shifts, I’ll get food and then just keep eating once I’m home. Like a whole takeout meal, then chips, sweets—whatever’s in the apartment. Afterwards I’m kind of shocked by how much I ate.
After one of these episodes where you eat a large amount, do you ever try to get rid of the food or make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?
Sometimes, yeah. After I’ve eaten all that, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just don’t want it sitting in me and turning into weight.
How often would you say these episodes of overeating followed by making yourself throw up have been happening, and for how many months has this been going on?

Since I got settled after moving apartments, it’s been most weeks—at least once a week. I’ll eat way more than I planned, then try to make up for it by throwing up, skipping breakfast, or making myself go for a long run.
About how many months has it been since these episodes—eating a large amount and then purging—started happening at least once a week?
About a year and five months, I think—since I moved into that temporary apartment near the tourist district.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food with a subjective sense of loss of control, occurring at least weekly for over a year. These binge episodes are followed by compensatory behaviors including self-induced vomiting, fasting (skipping breakfast), and excessive exercise (long runs) aimed at preventing weight gain. The frequency (≥1x/week) and duration (16 months, far exceeding the 3-month minimum) meet full DSM/ICD criteria for Bulimia Nervosa. There is no mention of significantly low body weight, which would suggest Anorexia Nervosa (binge-purge subtype) instead, and the pattern is well-defined and complete enough to not require an 'unspecified' or 'other' code.

confirmed_symptoms: Eating an objectively large amount of food (whole takeout meal plus chips and sweets) in a discrete period
Sense of being out of control/shocked by amount eaten after episodes
Episodes occurring at least once per week
Excessive exercise (long runs) to compensate for eating

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms (binge-purge cycle) have been occurring at least once weekly for approximately 16 months, since moving into a temporary apartment.
